focus_areas: Absence of Caliper: Confirming that no caliper is present and the dark shapes are internal vents.
Geometric integrity of the central hub bolts (look for non-hexagonal shapes).
Structural coherence of the background suspension parts (look for melting/fusion).
Consistency of the drilled hole patterns (look for warping or irregular spacing).
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Critically evaluate the absence of the caliper. The previous plan hallucinated a caliper; verify that the dark shapes are indeed internal rotor vents/holes. Use the open_vocabulary_detector to explicitly confirm no 'caliper' or 'hose' is detected. Pay close attention to the 'mechanical gibberish' in the background; use the geometric_depth_auditor to determine if this is a depth-map failure (bleeding) or simple out-of-focus blur. Scrutinize the central axle nut and bolts for geometric precision.
image_description: A close-up, high-angle view of a standalone metallic automotive brake rotor (disc). The rotor features a drilled and slotted surface pattern. The center hub shows mounting bolts and a central axle nut. Crucially, there is NO caliper assembly mounted on the rotor; the dark shapes visible are internal cooling vents or mounting apertures within the rotor hat, not an external caliper housing. The background contains blurred, indistinct mechanical components.
